value.text: GitHub issue link established during the pm-github pilot: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-todos/issues/49. Existing item covered the issue; import must update this item rather than create another.

message: Record GitHub provenance and duplicate-avoidance decision.

patch.value:
**Found by running the command against a real TODO file in a fresh, default workspace** — no unusual configuration involved.

## Reproduction

```bash
pm init td && pm install pm-todos
printf "# TODO\n\n- [x] Finished work that must not be lost\n- [ ] Pending work\n" > TODO.md

pm todos import TODO.md; echo "EXIT=$?"
pm list --status all
```

Result:

```
EXIT=0
imported: 1
 - open | Pending work
```

The completed item is **gone**. `Finished work that must not be lost` was never created, and the command reported success.

## What happens

stderr carries the cause, once per completed line:

```
TODO.md:3: create failed — Error: Close reason text is required because
governance.require_close_reason is enabled
```

The importer creates each item and, for a checked box, closes it — without supplying a close reason. `governance.require_close_reason` is a **built-in default**: it does not appear in a freshly written `.agents/pm/settings.json`, so this is the out-of-the-box path, not an opted-in strict mode.

## Why this is worse than a failed import

Three properties compound:

1. **It is the normal case.** A TODO file exists to track work; some of it is done. A file with no `[x]` lines is the unusual one.
2. **The import is partial, not refused.** Pending items are created, completed ones are dropped, and the workspace is left half-converted — the tracker and the file now disagree, and nothing records which lines were lost.
3. **Exit code 0.** Any agent or script that runs the import and checks the exit status sees success. The failure exists only in stderr text next to output that otherwise reads as a normal run.

The item dropped is specifically the record of **finished work**, which is the part a user cannot reconstruct by looking at what is left.

## Suggested fix

The close needs a reason. The natural one is available at the call site — the source line — so something like:

```ts
await client.close(id, "closed", {
  message: "Import completed TODO item",
  resolution: `Imported as completed from ${file}:${lineNumber}`,
});
```

Whatever text is chosen, two things matter beyond it:

- **Do not exit 0 on a partial import.** Either refuse the whole file before writing anything, or exit non-zero and name the lines that were dropped. A partial write reported as success is the part that turns a fixable bug into lost data.
- Worth checking `todos sync` for the same path, since it also reconciles completed state, and `todos export` for the inverse.

## Environment

`pm-todos` current `main`, `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.8.6/2026.8.7, fresh `pm init` workspace, Linux.
